subject: Latency buckets & hosting handoff — Cartwheel pilot next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Latency buckets & hosting handoff — Cartwheel pilot next steps

Hi Emma — great to meet you on the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have a clean handoff to your infra team: 

Summary of what we heard from Cartwheel:
- Primary feature: real-time personalized product recommendations for web and mobile checkout.
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~180 requests/sec (70% read-heavy), with 12% of traffic in a high-concurrency flash sale bucket that needs sub-50ms p95.
- Average request payload: small (<1KB); typical prompt length ~140 tokens; some longer background prompts for contextual signals.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII excluded from model inputs; logs retained per contract for 30 days.

Questions / asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the expected p95 target during normal and flash-sale windows? You mentioned 80ms day-to-day and <50ms for flash; want this in writing so we can validate the pilot SLA.
2) Please attach a 24-hour QPS sample (CSV) showing typical and peak-minute samples — that will let Solutions pick a deployment and sizing recommendation.
3) Will Cartwheel consider a dedicated pool for the flash-sale window (burst to reserved capacity) or do you prefer single-hosting model for simplicity?

Prelim recommendation (subject to QPS sample + security questionnaire):
- If p95 requirement is consistently <60ms for steady traffic and flash windows are rare (daily <1hr), we can likely satisfy via Hosted API with caching + hot-path routing.
- If flash windows are frequent and sustained or you need strict isolation for the flash pool, Dedicated capacity with a burst policy looks like the better path.

Attachments: I attached a one-pager on hosting options and a sample CSV template for QPS. Also linking our HubSpot record for the deal.

Next steps:
- Emma: please send the 24-hour QPS sample and confirm the p95 targets by EOD tomorrow.
- Ben/Karthik: once we get the sample, can you size a quick pilot estimate (cost and latency projections) and confirm if any on-prem private VPC constraints exist?

Thanks — GRACE

--
Grace O'Connor

Quick technical read on the attached QPS sample and recommended path: 

What I see:
- Baseline steady QPS ~180 req/sec with sustained short bursts up to ~650 req/sec for 8–12 minutes (2x in the 48h sample).
- Peak-minute concurrency during flash events pushes p50->p95 gap wide, which matches the need for a short-lived high-throughput, low-latency path.

Recommendation (pilot):
1) Pilot on Dedicated capacity with an autoscale-burst policy: reserve a smaller baseline pool (to control unit cost) and enable a burst to a pre-warmed dedicated slab during flash windows. This gives predictable p95 where it matters.
2) Implement prefix/KV caching for common prompts (recommend 120s TTL) to reduce token compute during repeat requests.
3) If Cartwheel prefers Hosted initially to reduce procurement friction, we can do a hybrid pilot: start Hosted with reserved warm workers for a 2-week pilot and measure p95 during the next scheduled flash event; if we miss the 45ms barrier, propose switching to Dedicated for the flash window.

Sizing notes (very rough):
- Baseline Dedicated: 6 GPUs (A100-like) with continuous batching tuned for 180 qps target.
- Burst slab: ability to add 18 GPUs for flash minutes (we can use pre-warm + fast routing).

I'll draft a short cost comparison and a one-page runbook for switching modes during flash events. Grace — can you confirm procurement contact and any required procure timelines?

Ben
